quiz.question: What is a sign of a Liskov Substitution Principle (LSP) violation?

answers.answer: When a subclass performs better than its superclass
When a subclass requires type checks to work properly
When a superclass has more methods than its subclass
When a subclass adds new methods that are never used

quiz.question: In the provided Dart example, which behavior indicates an LSP violation?

answers.answer: The Penguin class does not implement any new methods
The fly method in Penguin calls the superclass's method
The Penguin class overrides fly and throws an exception not present in Bird
The Bird class has more overridden methods than the Penguin class

quiz.question: Why is substituting 'Penguin' for 'Bird' a violation of LSP in the given example?

answers.answer: Because Penguin adds new flying capabilities to Bird
Because Penguin instances exhibit unexpected behavior compared to Bird when flying
Because both Penguin and Bird have the same properties and methods
Because Penguin can live in different climates compared to other Birds
